about: Which placement survives an import and which may be thrown away. A consumer cannot tell by looking at the collection kind, so the producer declares it.

when.importInto: a tool with no matrix view

cases.why: The region is a judgment the user made about the task, stored as a position. A tool that draws no grid must still keep the value and report that it cannot display it. Dropping it destroys the only record of the assessment.

Canvas coordinates are furniture — where the user dragged something on one particular day. Discarding them loses nothing, and an import that reports reduced fidelity here will train users to ignore the warning that matters.

expect.reason: semantic placement must use named regions, not coordinates

cases.why: A coordinate is meaningless outside the grid that produced it — the same point means different things at different zoom levels and window sizes. 'urgent-important' opens correctly in a tool that renders a plain list.
A kanban column is usually status wearing a position. Flattening the board loses the status of every card on it, which is the entire content of a board.

When a board's columns are generated from a status field the objects already carry, the column is a rendering of data held elsewhere and carries nothing of its own. Same kind, opposite answer — which is exactly why the collection kind cannot be trusted to imply the semantics.

Ordering tokens sort byte-wise, not numerically or by locale. Under a language-aware collation 'Zz' sorts after 'a0' and the top of every list is wrong. Do not parse these as numbers and do not re-generate them on import.
